subject: Feasibility & timeline: combined GLBA + BAA addenda for Trinity Bank
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@trinitybank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: Addenda feasibility — GLBA + BAA for Trinity Bank / pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. As discussed, Trinity would like to run a short feasibility check for two specific items tied to our pilot: 1) GLBA addendum language around financial data handling, and 2) a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for a subset of health-related data we may surface through one workflow.

I've attached an annotated list of DPA questions and a short spreadsheet that summarizes what we're expecting from vendors. High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood can sign a GLBA addendum and a BAA (or a combined addendum) under the hosted API offering, and separately under a Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Subprocessor list and whether any subprocessors handle tokenized or raw inputs.
- Data residency and routing (we prefer US-only for Trinity customer data in this pilot).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption in transit/rest, and KMS/HSM options.
- A rough timeline for legal redlines and procurement (we're aiming to finalize vendor on or before 2027-07-01).

Can you confirm who on your side owns the legal/compliance asks and whether you can share a draft redline timeline? We would appreciate a short call (30 min) in the next few business days to align scope.

Attachments: Trinity_DPA_Questions_Annotated.pdf (220KB), BAA_Reqs_Summary.xlsx (45KB)

Thanks,
Samantha Lowe
Senior Counsel, Vendor Risk
Trinity Bank
Samantha.Lowe@trinitybank.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@trinitybank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Addenda feasibility — GLBA + BAA for Trinity Bank / pilot

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detail and the attachments. Looping in Marcus (compliance ops) and Monica (legal) so we can confirm feasibility and a timeline.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- Monica will lead the contractual redline for both the GLBA addendum and the BAA; she can produce a first pass redline within 3 business days for hosted API and a second pass for Dedicated/Private options.
- Marcus will validate the technical controls (subprocessors, residency, and encryption) and confirm whether any current subprocessors would touch the pilot data.
- I'll coordinate a short 30-min alignment call. Proposed time: Thursday 2027-06-17 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you?

Preliminary notes:
- Hosted API: we generally support GLBA commitments in our DPA and can sign tailored addenda for regulated financial customers; for BAAs we typically require programmatic segregation or a Dedicated/Private deployment for full control over PHI flows, depending on the dataset.
- Subprocessors: we have a standard list (I will ask Marcus to attach the current roster) — note that some managed infra providers will have visibility into encrypted payloads only if you choose to share keys.

I attached an internal working draft (BAA-draft-TRN-v1.docx) to accelerate Monica's redline.

If you can confirm the sample dataset scope (which fields are PHI vs. financial), that will help speed the BAA decision.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
(650) 555-0114

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@trinitybank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Addenda feasibility — GLBA + BAA for Trinity Bank / pilot

Samantha — quick technical follow-up to support Vanessa & Monica's timeline.

On data residency and subprocessors:
- We can isolate pilot traffic to US regions (Redwood-hosted regions in us-west2/us-east1) and restrict routing via policy. For Dedicated or Private deployments, residency can be enforced at the VPC level.
- Current subprocessors that could see token-level data in hosted mode: managed GPU infra partner (GPUI Inc.) and our monitoring vendor (LogFetch). Both handle encrypted payloads by default; only LogFetch processes metadata (latency/trace) unless you enable detailed telemetry.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted API supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration but is subject to onboarding time (2-3 weeks).

On BAA feasibility:
- If the dataset contains regulated PHI (as defined by HIPAA) in transmission to the model, we strongly recommend Dedicated or Private deployment for the pilot. In hosted API we can accept certain PHI classes with a BAA if controls and routing are tightly scoped, but it increases the compliance and operational checklist (audit logging, retention, and export controls).

Needed from your side to fast-track:
1) Data flow diagram showing which fields are PHI and which are financial-only.
2) Confirmation whether Trinity requires customer-managed keys.
3) Any mandatory subprocessors Trinity will not accept (we can evaluate replacements).

I'll attach the latest subprocessor roster and our SOC 2 Type II cover page in the follow-up.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@trinitybank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial: Addenda feasibility — GLBA + BAA for Trinity Bank / pilot

Vanessa / Marcus / Monica — thanks for the quick responses and the proposed timeline. The call on Thursday at 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Can your legal team share a redline for the GLBA addendum and the BAA draft by EOD Friday (2027-06-18)? Procurement wants to see vendor redlines before we circle back internally.
- We will provide a short data flow diagram by end of day Wednesday (2027-06-16).
- Procurement timeline: we are aiming to issue a PO by 2027-07-01 if the terms are acceptable; if redlines slip beyond 2027-06-25 that will push our internal approvals.

I've attached our procurement timeline for visibility.

Attachments: procurement_timeline.pdf (38KB)

Talk on Thursday — Samantha
